title: Editorial: Genomic Assessment of Adaptive Potential of Populations to Environmental Challenges: Applications to Management and Conservation
content:
ABSTRACT

Rapid environmental change poses unprecedented challenges for species persistence, threatening not only population size but the genomic adaptive variation required for evolutionary responses. Understanding this adaptive potential is crucial for effective management and conservation strategies, as it determines a population's capacity to cope with current and future climate shifts, habitat loss, emerging diseases and other environmental pressures. This Special Issue is therefore timely in the context of advancing genetic diversity monitoring recommendations (e.g., UN Convention on Biological Diversity Target 4), bringing together 40 original papers, perspectives and reviews that link genomic insights to conservation status and practice. The contributions span empirical studies, mechanistic investigations, theoretical frameworks and applied case studies. Together, these studies highlight how genomic approaches can illuminate the mechanisms and distribution of adaptive variation and inform strategies to maintain population resilience and guide effective management under environmental change.
